prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity desktop web application comp, 16:10 landscape
Primary request: Design the first viewport of regressio, a browser validation dashboard for a TypeScript statistics library. This is an OPERATE interface, not a marketing poster. The visual world is a precision pen-plotter acceptance sheet.
Structure: a slim instrument header across the top; below it a dominant regression plot taking roughly two thirds of the width; a narrow vertical proof rail on the right; a ruled family-tab strip along the bottom edge. The plot contains labeled synthetic observations, an OLS line, a polynomial curve, a robust line, residual stems, axes, calibration ticks, and a visible small plotter carriage resting at the end of the active blue trace. The proof rail shows clear readable values: 36 / 36 APIs, WASM ACTIVE, 0 FAILED, and a runtime. Bottom tabs read REGRESSION, CLASSIFICATION, DIAGNOSTICS, PREPROCESSING, INTERVALS, MATRIX.
Text (verbatim): regressio; Browser proof suite; Synthetic dataset; 36 / 36 APIs; WASM ACTIVE; 0 FAILED.
Style/medium: exceptional production-grade interface mockup; cool drafting-paper white ground, graphite rules and annotations, saturated ultramarine plotter ink, safety orange used only for exception marks; technical condensed sans labels and tabular monospaced numerals; registration marks, crop marks, tiny coordinates, precise vector plots. No rounded card grid. No glass, no gradients, no 3D, no photography.
Composition/framing: flat straight-on screenshot, full browser viewport, asymmetrical proof-sheet composition, generous quiet margins around the single dominant plot, crisp legible interface details.
Constraints: the visitor must instantly understand that real statistical functions are running and passing in-browser; results and navigation must be accessible and plausible; no invented customers, benchmarks, prices, or testimonials; no logos besides the lowercase regressio wordmark; no watermark.
selectionReason: Strongest visual proof: the dominant chart, right proof rail, and family index explain the product in one scan. User delegated the visual choice.
